brief: GS raised its Fed call to hikes (from a prior no-hike forecast) on three drivers: Middle East escalation pushing refined product prices to 2022 highs, Q3 GDP tracking 3.3% with August payrolls +162k, and August CPI/PPI implying core PCE +0.27% m/m, above pre-CPI expectations. GS expects the hawkish news to fade: oil exports have recovered to ~80% of prewar volumes despite the Strait of Hormuz closure, China has curtailed imports since August, and GS projects Brent falling to $85/barrel by December, though product prices stay elevated on refining shortages. US growth is bifurcated (strong upper-income/AI sectors, weak housing) and GS expects consumer spending to soften despite firm August retail sales. Core PCE, though it picked up sequentially in August, has slowed to 2.5% annualized over three months as tariff, energy, and software-price impulses fade. GS sees 2.2% by 2027Q4. The FOMC hiked 25bp unanimously and 16 of 18 participants signaled another hike, which GS expects in October. Beyond that GS sees a stable rate, then cuts to 3.25-3.5% starting late 2027.
